strategies.summary: Replace each Conv2dâBatchNorm2dâReLU sequence with a fused CUDA kernel that reads conv output once, computes BN normalization (using stored running_mean/running_var in inference mode), applies the affine transform, and writes the ReLU-clamped result. Eliminates two full tensor round-trips to global memory per fused triple.
implementation_hints: In inference mode BatchNorm reduces to a per-channel scale/bias: out = relu((x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) * weight + bias). Precompute fused_scale = weight / sqrt(var + eps) and fused_bias = bias - mean * fused_scale on the host before the kernel launch.
Write a 1-D element-wise CUDA kernel parameterized by (C, HW) that loads x[n,c,hw], applies fused_scale[c] and fused_bias[c], then max(0, result). Use __ldg for the scale/bias arrays.
Bind the kernel via pybind11; call it from forward_stmt_2 (after conv1) and forward_stmt_8 (after conv_final) using the precomputed fused parameters stored as buffers in init_body.
Use vectorized loads (float4) when HW is divisible by 4 to improve memory bandwidth utilization.
Keep the BN modules registered so state_dict compatibility is preserved; just bypass their forward() call and use their buffers directly.
strategies.expected_gain: 15â25% latency reduction on the two stem/head conv+BN+ReLU triples; memory traffic cut by ~2x for those ops.
risk_notes: Must use running_mean/running_var (eval-mode statistics), not compute live statistics â model must be in eval() mode.
Precomputed fused_scale/fused_bias must be recomputed if BN weights are updated (training step); safe for inference-only benchmarking.
Output dtype and shape must remain identical to nn.BatchNorm2d output.

Do not alter conv weight layout or introduce im2col rewrites here.

Add torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True in init_body (or once globally) so cuDNN profiles algorithm selection on the first run.
Ensure the output tensor in forward_stmt_12 is returned as contiguous if downstream code expects NCHW: return x.contiguous() or leave as-is if caller is flexible.
This is a pure Python-level change requiring no custom CUDA kernel â cuda_cu and cuda_cpp anchors remain empty, making this a low-risk baseline improvement.
strategies.expected_gain: 10â20% speedup from cuDNN NHWC conv kernels; larger relative gains on depthwise convolutions which are especially sensitive to layout.
risk_notes: channels_last layout affects tensor strides, not values â numerical output is identical.
benchmark=True adds a one-time warmup cost on first forward; acceptable for benchmarking scenarios.
Some PyTorch versions have edge cases with channels_last and certain grouped/depthwise conv configurations â validate correctness.

Precompute fused_scale and fused_bias for every BN in every MBConv block during __init__ (or lazily on first forward) and store as non-parameter buffers.

risk_notes: MBConv blocks contain skip connections; ensure the residual add is still performed correctly after fusing BN into the main branch only.
ReLU6 clamping must match PyTorch's min(max(x,0),6) exactly.
If the model is ever put in training mode, the fused kernel path must be disabled and standard nn.BatchNorm2d used.

Do not alter depthwise conv grouping or kernel geometry.
Do not hardcode channel counts â parameterize the kernel by C.

review_notes.claude-compatible: High-leverage target since MBConv blocks dominate runtime and each contains 2-3 BN+activation sequences. Fusing depthwise-conv BN+ReLU6 chains is sound. Score docked one point because the implementation requires wrapping Sequential modules and handling residual add boundaries correctly, which adds meaningful correctness risk. The ReLU6 clamping parity and training-mode fallback requirements add implementation surface area.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Assumes inference mode by precomputing scale/bias from running stats. If the benchmark requires training mode or exact statistic computation (as hinted by the semantic profile), this will fail correctness.

strategies.summary: Replace the AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1,1)) â flatten â Linear sequence with a single fused CUDA kernel that reduces the spatial dimensions of the feature map, accumulates into a 1-D vector, and immediately applies the linear projection (WÂ·x + b) in one pass. This eliminates the intermediate (B, C, 1, 1) allocation and the separate GEMM dispatch overhead for the small final linear.
implementation_hints: Input is (2, 1408, H, W) after the final conv+BN+ReLU; for EfficientNetB2 with 224Ã224 input the spatial size at this point is 7Ã7, so HW=49 â small enough to reduce entirely in shared memory.

One CUDA block per (batch, output_class) pair: load the 1408-element pooled vector once into shared memory, then each thread computes a partial dot product with the corresponding row of the FC weight matrix.

Alternatively, use one block per batch item that computes the spatial average over 1408Ã49 elements and writes a (B, 1408) intermediate, then call cublasSgemm for the linear â this is lower risk and still removes the flatten allocation.
The fused avgpoolâflatten kernel should write a contiguous (B, 1408) float tensor directly, which cublas can consume without reshape.
Export the avgpool+flatten kernel as a single pybind11 entrypoint; replace forward_stmt_9 and forward_stmt_10 with one call, keep forward_stmt_11 as self.fc.
strategies.expected_gain: Small absolute gain (~2â5 ms) but removes kernel launch overhead and intermediate allocation for the tail; improves memory efficiency for batched inference.
risk_notes: Output of the fused avgpool+flatten must be exactly numerically equivalent to AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1,1)) followed by flatten(1) â verify with unit test.
FC weight is (num_classes, 1408); ensure matrix orientation matches cublas column-major convention if using cublas for the projection step.
For batch size 2 and 1000 classes the full fused avgpool+linear kernel is tiny â cuBLAS is likely faster than a hand-rolled kernel for the GEMM part.

Do not fuse the FC weight update into the kernel â keep fc as an nn.Linear for parameter management.
Do not emit a (B, C, 1, 1) intermediate tensor if the full fusion is implemented.

review_notes.openai-compatible: Tail fusion is technically feasible but likely low payoff versus complexity; hand-rolled fusion around the final FC is easy to underperform cuBLAS and is only loosely connected to the normalization optimization target.
review_notes.claude-compatible: The fused avgpool+flatten+FC kernel targets a portion of the network that accounts for a small fraction of total runtime. The analysis correctly notes the gain is only 2-5ms. The cublas integration for a (2, 1000) x (1000, 1408) GEMM adds complexity without proportional benefit. Shared-memory reduction over 1408x49 elements per block is feasible but over-engineered for this tail. Better to use strategy_08's simpler mean() replacement and keep fc as nn.Linear.
